tweets: Why your peptide vendor disappeared overnight — the 503A compounding crackdown, what's still legal, and where the gray market went. Thread on the regulatory shift most peptide buyers missed:

1/ The FDA’s 503A compounding framework is the *only* legal pathway for peptide therapies in the US outside of clinical trials. No, research peptides don’t count. No, telemedicine doesn’t bypass it. Vendors pretending otherwise got shut down hard this year.

2/ 503A means physician-supervised, patient-specific prescriptions from licensed compounding pharmacies. Not 'research use' vials. Not bulk imports. Not 'wellness peptides' with a checkbox disclaimer. The crackdown targeted anyone blurring these lines.

3/ What survived? Legit telehealth operations with: - Actual clinician review - Compounding pharmacy partners - No blanket protocols - Labs/follow-up when indicated The gray market just got gray-er (and riskier) for buyers.

4/ The compliance cost is real: proper 503A means no 'peptide of the month' clubs, no unlimited refills, no one-click peptides. But it’s the only model that doesn’t end with a warning letter or worse. We built VendraRx to operate in the white space.
